1 نَآءَ , aor. يَنِىْءُ, (so in the S, Nh, L, Msb; but in some copies of the K, يناءُ, [which appears to be put by mistake for the inf. n. in the acc. case];) inf. n. نَىْءٌ, (S,) and نَىٌّ, without ء, and نَوْءٌ, (Sh,) It (flesh meat, &c.) was not, or did not become, sufficiently cooked; it was insufficiently cooked: (S, K:) (like نَهِئَ:) or it was untouched by fire; (i. e., raw]. (L.) ―
-b2- It (a thing) was not firmly, not soundly, not thoroughly, done. [See 4.] (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
